nodes.recap: Corolla wakes - anxious bedside, Theo on the tech, console left unsolved as a hook

dialogues.precomment:
She comes around half an hour after the lighthouse.##

The first thing she sees is all of them leaning over her bunk,
faces anxious in varying degrees of composure.# Smiurl has apparently
been self-appointed as chief nurse and is the closest.#
Efeliah has already cleaned and bandaged the wound across the old burn-scar.
Outside, through the porthole, open water.##

Corolla blinks.# Takes in the ceiling, composite material, pale, no
ship-timber or salvaged wood, and the clean white light of the recessed fixtures.#
Then she looks at the faces above her and does what she does.
dialogues.line: I'm fine.
dialogues.comment:
She says it the way you'd say it if you were trying to convince yourself
as much as the room.

dialogues.line:
You were fantastic.# Ef described everything we couldn't see.##
You used the dwarf's back as a launch ramp.
dialogues.comment: She almost laughs.# Not quite, but almost.

dialogues.line:
She's also bandaged your wound!# The medicines on board are extraordinary!#
She says they'll work wonders even after all this time!
dialogues.comment: He is practically glowing with the satisfaction of having useful information to deliver.

dialogues.line:
The ship's medical stores are very well preserved.# You'll be on your feet
within the day if you rest.

dialogues.precomment:
Corolla glances around the cabin: the smooth walls, the recessed lights,
the clean lines of a technology from another world entirely.
dialogues.line: What... is this ship?

dialogues.precomment:
Theo, standing in the doorway, which he barely fits in,
has the look of a man who has just been given an enormous gift and is not
entirely sure what to do with the feeling.
dialogues.line:
Solar energy.# The sails collect sunlight, feed electric motors below the waterline.#
Electric motors.# We had examples of this technology at Øder,
but very few.# Very limited examples.#
Nothing like this.
dialogues.comment:
He looks over his shoulder, back at the ship around him,
with an expression you rarely see on Theo's face: something close to wonder.

dialogues.precomment: She asks it with her eyes still on the ceiling, half a smile in it.
dialogues.line: ...and who's at the helm?

dialogues.precomment: Theo's satisfaction dims, just a little.
dialogues.line:
I found the console at the stern.# There's a script on it I don't recognize.#
Not yours, not ours.# There seemed to be enough there to work something out,
so I tried.# I can't tell you if it's right.
dialogues.comment:
He says it plainly, the way he says most things.# But you catch,
underneath it, something that in anyone else you would call embarrassment.

dialogues.precomment: He looks at you, which from Theo counts as a direct request.
dialogues.line: We are sailing somewhere.# I would rather it were south.
I'll go take a look.
dialogues.comment:
Corolla's eyes are already closing.##

$R"Don't let me sleep too long."$C##

Smiurl immediately sets about arranging himself in the chair beside her bunk
with the air of someone who has been waiting for a job.

nodes.recap: the console puzzle - examine sails/helm/observation screens for clues, then enter the heading
nodes.text:
You leave Corolla to Smiurl's enthusiastic nursing and go looking for Theo's console.##

The main cabin runs most of the hull's length below deck: pale walls,
smooth and unscratched, narrow bunks folded into alcoves, light coming
from fixtures with no visible source.# At the stern end, a panel of
switches waits, dark until you get close, and then the whole board lights
at once, amber characters in a script that means nothing to you.##

There is a lot of ship to get lost in before you trust yourself with that panel.

actions.answer: There's plenty else on this ship worth a look before you trust that panel.

objects.answer:
You climb back on deck for a proper look.# Broad, layered panels of some
dark material, catching what little afternoon light there is, and as you
watch, one shifts a few degrees on its mount, unhurried, tracking the sun
the way a flower does.##

Down at the base of the mast, a small plate glows the same amber as the
console below, one symbol only, worn smooth by a thousand hands that were
never yours.# Whatever it means, it means the sun.

At the stern, behind the console, sits an old-style helm: an actual wheel,
spoked and worn, usable by hand if you ever wanted to steer this thing
yourself.# Set into the deck below it, a compass rose, tarnished but
legible, an old script you can almost place.# North, south, and the
ordinal points between them, exactly where you would expect to find them
on a wheel that looks like nothing else on this ship.

Forward, the compartment with the glass floor holds a bank of screens
along one wall: seabed readings, a slow procession of marine life
drifting past unseen cameras, and one display given over entirely to a
small blinking mark trailing a thin line behind it, back the way you
came.# North, if the mark means what you think it means, and the line
runs off the edge of the screen in the one direction you already know.

Up close, the amber script resolves into clusters of symbols arranged in
a ring around a single dial, with a lever beneath it that clearly wants
pulling once the dial is set.# Somewhere in that ring, one cluster means
south.# You just have to work out which.

Three more cabins line the corridor, each with its own narrow bunk and
its own set of ship's amenities.# It resembles nothing so much as a rich
man's pleasure yacht, borrowed from a much richer century.

Down a ladder through a hatch in the floor, a dining area opens up: a
galley at the stern end, a scatter of tables and chairs, and
floor-to-ceiling portholes on either side through which the sea outside
is somehow more visible than the sea usually is.# You try to find the
bottom with your eyes, and fail.

actions.answer:
Enter what, exactly?# You will want to know what you are setting before
you touch that dial.

condition.refusal:
You turn the dial to a cluster of symbols that looks close enough.#
On deck, the sails give an uncertain shudder and start folding in on
themselves; the ship yaws a few degrees and settles, entirely
unconvinced.# Whatever you just told it, the ship doesn't like it.

objects.answer:
$c<<Sun, north, and a line pointing the way you came.# That should be
enough to find south.>>$C##

You turn the dial until it settles on the cluster of symbols opposite the
one glowing at the base of the mast, and pull the lever beneath it.##

Somewhere below, something changes pitch.# On deck, the sails swing
together, smooth and certain this time, and hold.##

Theo appears at the top of the ladder, looks at the board, then at you,
and something in his face that you have not seen before settles into
place.##

$B"You had it."$C# he says, and for Theo that is practically a cheer.

nodes.recap: setting sail - Corolla at the stern as land disappears
nodes.text:
By the time Corolla has rested and is back on her feet, ignoring everyone
who suggests she rest longer, the coastal town is far behind
and the open sea is in every direction.##

The sails track the sun with a slow, almost imperceptible patience,
rotating a few degrees as the afternoon moves,
the way a flower tilts its face without appearing to move at all.#
The motors push the hull through calm water with a low, clean vibration
that you feel more than hear, and the ship eases through the sea
without drama, the bow leaving a long white line.##

Corolla stands at the stern for a while, watching the last suggestion of land
sink below the horizon.# She says nothing, but after a moment
her shoulders drop a fraction, and she breathes slowly out through her nose,
and you realize this is the closest she will come to relief.##

nodes.recap: the Edzzen following on their own ships - then they fall behind
nodes.text:
The Edzzen have not given up.##

Looking back through a glass of Theo's finding, you can see them:
two or three old vessels, sails filled, making what speed they can
in the direction the solar ship has taken.# They are not slow, exactly,
but they are no match for electric motors and a hull built
for open ocean, and Theo watches them for a while through the glass
and then sets it down.##

$B"They won't catch us.# We're pulling away."$C##

You say nothing.# You watch the smudge of their sails on the horizon
until they vanish, and feel a relief so specific that it almost has a name.##

nodes.recap: Efeliah's ocean meditation, pt.1 - the chorus beneath the sea, reply picks how Kriss responds

dialogues.precomment:
On the second evening at sea, the sun goes down ahead of you,
painting the water in wide bands of copper and rose.# The others are below,
and Efeliah is sitting cross-legged at the very front of the prow deck,
directly above the glass floor of the observation room, her eyes closed.#
You come to sit beside her.##

She does not open her eyes, but she smiles.
dialogues.line: I am listening.
To what?

The sea.# Its depths.#
On Noi-Hert, the sea is far more populous than the land.#
Fish of every kind, invertebrates, micro-organisms, great mammoths of the deep...#
Listening to their minds is like hearing a chorus of vibrations
on every frequency from the highest to the lowest,
every creature participating, building into one vast field of mental energy
below the level of the sea.#
If you could see it...
dialogues.comment: She pauses, and the pause has a kind of reverence in it.

dialogues.line: It would be a superb sight.

replies.line: Ask her to share it with you.

dialogues.precomment:
You look at the water spreading around you in every direction.
You cannot hear what she describes, or not exactly, but there is something:
a faint, sourceless sense of presence, vast and unhurried,
moving underneath the surface like a tide that has nothing to do with the moon.
dialogues.line: Can you try to share it with me?# What you're hearing?

dialogues.precomment:
You say nothing.# You only watch the water, and let the quiet stretch
between you, and try, without much hope, to catch some fraction of what
she is describing.

dialogues.line: You don't have to ask.# I heard the question before you shaped it.
dialogues.comment: There is warmth in it, and no mockery at all.

nodes.recap: why she can't transmit it - Kriss's homesickness, reply picks how he lets it out

dialogues.line:
Your mind, though exceptional, is not naturally receptive in the way
that nearly all minds I have encountered on Noi-Hert are.#
Sometimes you have spikes of energy and catch external images,
but you are not made for this.#
The only hope you have of understanding what lives in your mind
is to follow this pull that has guided you so far.
dialogues.comment: She opens her eyes and looks at you.# The light on the water.

replies.line: Admit you would rather just go home.
Try to make a joke of it instead.

dialogues.precomment:
You look at the water, and the light on it, and the deepening sky.#
No joke quite manages to cover it, and something comes up that you have
been pushing down for some time.
dialogues.line:
Honestly?# I don't much care what's in my head.#
I just want to go home.
dialogues.comment:
You say it quietly, and then you are surprised to find that your eyes
have filled without your permission, which is not the effect you were looking for.##

dialogues.line:
Perhaps you will find an answer to that too.#
We don't know what awaits us.# You'll see.# It will all work out.
dialogues.comment:
But even as she says it, she is thinking something she does not transmit:
that she cannot begin to comprehend how she can say those words
to someone who is light-years from his planet and millennia from his time.##

She closes her eyes.# She keeps her arm around your shoulders.#
You look out into the ocean depths of this strange planet while the last
of the sun goes below the horizon and the stars come out, one by one.##

nodes.recap: evening in the cabin - companionship at sea

dialogues.precomment:
That night, with the ship running steadily south under a sky thick with stars,
all five of you are in the main cabin.# The navigation computer tends the course.
There is food from the ship's stores, preserved, more varied and less grim
than anything you have eaten in weeks.# Efeliah has found a sealed container
of something that might be wine and is examining it with quiet curiosity.
dialogues.line: Do you think there are things in the water?# Big things?
dialogues.comment:
He is staring at the glass floor of the forward compartment.
His skin is a mild, curious amber.

dialogues.line:
Statistically, yes.# The southern sea is deep and cold,
and everything I have heard in it suggests fauna of considerable size.
dialogues.comment: She finally opens the container and sniffs it, and her eyebrows rise.

dialogues.line: I was hoping you would say no.
dialogues.comment: He shifts slightly away from the glass floor.

dialogues.precomment: Corolla is lying on one of the bunks, one arm behind her head.
dialogues.line: Ef, stop torturing the dwarf and open the bottle.
It may be two hundred years old.
dialogues.comment:
She pours some into a cup and passes it to Corolla,
who drinks without ceremony and hands it back.

dialogues.line: It's fine.# Very fine, actually.
dialogues.comment: She stares at the ceiling for a moment, then, quietly:

dialogues.line: I did not expect us to make it this far.
dialogues.comment:
Nobody speaks for a moment.# It is not a complaint,
but simply the truth, offered plainly,
the way Corolla sometimes offers things when her guard slips.

replies.line: Say nothing, and let it sit.
Tell her you didn't expect it either.

dialogues.precomment: Theo, sitting with his back against the hull and his eyes half-closed, says:
dialogues.line: We keep going.
dialogues.comment: It is not a reassurance, but a statement of fact, the way gravity is a fact.

dialogues.precomment: Corolla turns her head and looks at him.
dialogues.line: Yeah.
dialogues.comment:
She says it softly, and looks back at the ceiling.##

Smiurl has fallen asleep sitting up,
leaning against Efeliah's shoulder, his face entirely unguarded,
and Efeliah looks at him with quiet fondness and does not move.

nodes.recap: three days of peace at sea
nodes.text:
Three days pass like something out of a dream you did not know you were allowed to have.##

The sea is calm, the sails track the sun with their slow mechanical patience,
and the navigation computer adjusts course twice a day with soft chirps that bother no one.#
You sleep in an actual bunk, between actual walls,
without one ear listening for the sound of footsteps in the dark.##

You talk, all of you, in various combinations, about nothing in particular.#
Efeliah tells you about Seer's Rock, about the library of stone-tablet Memories,
about the Master's belief that the mind was not separate from the universe
but simply a finer arrangement of it.#
Corolla teaches you a card game using a deck improvised from torn scraps
of the ship's technical manual, and she cheats badly and dares you to call her on it.#
Smiurl gets seasick on the second day, recovers on the third,
and spends the fourth leaning over the prow, watching the water,
his skin a meditative pale blue.##

Efeliah listens to the chorus, and you watch her listen,
and the peace on her face is something you want to remember.##

nodes.recap: storm approaches - sky darkens - Theo's order to secure the ship
nodes.text:
On the morning of the fifth day, the horizon ahead turns the color of a bruise.##

It happens gradually at first.#
The blue-white sky thickens to a hazier white,
then to a flat gray that strips the water of its glitter and leaves it leaden and cold,
and the swells grow, not dramatically but steadily,
the ship beginning to lift and dip on rollers that are still comfortable but no longer gentle.#
The sails retract automatically, folding themselves inward with a mechanical whisper
that sounds, in the new silence, like a held breath.##

The navigation console emits a series of chirps
and then a sustained tone that Efeliah identifies,
after some study of the screen's amber characters,
as a storm alert.##

$c<<Of course.# Of course there is a storm.
We were having a nice time,
which historically has been the universe's preferred trigger.>>#

$CTheo looks at the sky, then at the console, and does the math out loud.##

$B"There's little the computer can do about this.# Without sun the motors'
charge won't hold, and if the wind picks up we could lose the sails
outright."$C##

He is already moving, hauling the rope locker shut, checking the deck for
anything that isn't fixed down.##

$B"Get below.# Bring anything loose that could be lost, and bring it now.#
We won't have time later."$C##

You have maybe a few minutes before the weather takes the choice away from you.##

nodes.recap: storm prep A - medbay vs galley, real cost, gates c19 supplies
nodes.text: There isn't time for everything.# You have to choose.

choices.desc: Get to the medical bay, and lash down the medicines before they shatter.
Get to the galley, and save what food and water you can reach.

nodes.recap: medbay secured - galley lost
nodes.text:
You throw yourself down the ladder into the medical bay and start
strapping down cabinets, jars, the sealed cases of instruments,
working fast while the deck tilts under you more with every passing minute.##

You hear, from further down the hull, the unmistakable sound of things
breaking loose in the galley: glass, tins, whatever Efeliah didn't
have time to reach.# There is nothing to be done about it now.##

You finish, breathless, everything in the medical bay lashed as tight
as you can manage, and haul yourself back toward the ladder.##

nodes.recap: galley secured - medbay lost
nodes.text:
You throw yourself down the ladder toward the galley and grab
what you can reach: the water canisters, sealed tins, a net bag
of something dense and durable-looking, jamming it all into a locker
and wedging the locker shut with your own boots.##

Somewhere behind you, in the medical bay, you hear the specific,
unmistakable sound of glass breaking against a wall, more than once.#
Efeliah's medicines, unattended.# There is nothing to be done about it now.##

You finish, breathless, and haul yourself back toward the ladder.##

nodes.recap: storm prep B - Corolla vs rigging, real cost
nodes.text:
On deck, the wind has already found a new register, higher and meaner.#
Theo is fighting the last of the rigging alone, and Corolla, half-dressed
and furious about it, has appeared at the top of the ladder insisting
she's fine to help.##

choices.desc: Go make Corolla lie back down. She won't listen to anyone else.
Stay topside, and help Theo finish the rigging instead.

nodes.recap: Corolla secured - rigging left half-done
nodes.text:
You go to her, and it costs you most of what patience you have left,
but you get an arm under hers and walk her bodily back to her bunk,
over every objection she has, which are numerous and creative.##

Behind you, above, you hear Theo working alone, and later,
when you finally climb back up, you find a length of loose cable
still snapping in the wind that he never had the extra hands to secure.##

$R"I could have helped,"$C# she says, from the bunk, not quite meeting your eyes.##

$c"I know,"$C# you say.# $c"That's why I did it."$C##

nodes.recap: rigging secured - Efeliah handles Corolla instead
nodes.text:
You stay, and between you and Theo the last of the exposed gear
gets lashed down or hauled below in something close to good order.##

Corolla is still arguing from the top of the ladder when Efeliah
finally appears behind her, says something too quiet for you to hear,
and walks her back down by the elbow without further protest.##

$B"Good,"$C# Theo says, of the rigging, which from him is a commendation.##

nodes.recap: storm worsens - real danger
nodes.text:
By midday, there is no question about it anymore.##

The swells are three meters, then four,
and the ship climbs each one in a long, lunging motion
and comes down the far side with a crash that sends water sheeting across the deck.#
The sky has closed completely, a low ceiling of boiling gray-black
that flickers with interior light, and the wind has gone from a whisper to a roar,
and when it hits you in the face it carries water, not spray but solid,
pelting rain that strikes with unexpected force.##

Smiurl is below, and everyone not needed on deck is below,
while Corolla and Theo are lashed to the stern rail,
fighting the wheel in turns as the computer struggles
with a sea that no longer follows any of its models.#
The masts creak, and something deep in the hull makes a sound
that you do not want to interpret.##

$c<<We are going to lose this ship.#
I know it with the bone-cold certainty of someone who has already lost
several things on this planet and developed an instinct for it.>>$C##

nodes.recap: the decisive wave - ship goes down
nodes.text:
The wave that decides it comes out of the dark.##

You see it for perhaps two seconds before it hits,
a black wall of water, twice the height of the mast,
carrying the low groaning sound of something vast being moved against its will.#
There is no time to shout.#
Theo lets go of the wheel and throws himself flat,
and Corolla grabs the rail with both hands and locks her elbows.##

The wave takes the ship broadside.###

The world becomes white and cold and violent and there is no up.#
The deck tilts past ninety degrees and you are not on it anymore,
you are in the water, and the water is black and enormous and full of noise.#
Something hits you, a piece of the ship, the mast, you do not know,
and the noise cuts out.##

nodes.recap: underwater - which way is up - the cue is his own weight
nodes.text:
You are underwater.##

You know this because of the cold and the silence and the burning in your lungs,
which have apparently made the executive decision to remind you they exist.#
The water is dark, no light in any direction, no surface visible,
and you do not know which way is up.##

There is nothing down here to steer by, no glimmer, no sound with a direction
in it, nothing at all except your own weight, which is the only thing left
in this whole black ocean that still knows something you don't.##

Your body wants to panic.# You are familiar with this impulse,
and you do not have the time for it.##
nodes.alttext:
You are still underwater, and there is a good deal less of you
than there was a moment ago.##

No light.# No surface.# No air worth the name.#
And your own weight, patient as ever, still trying to tell you something.##

choices.desc: Go still, and let your body find its own buoyancy.
Kick hard, any direction. Up is probably one of them.

nodes.recap: wrong choice - kicked downward, costs the last of his air, routes back into 18
nodes.text:
You kick, hard, because doing something is always easier than doing nothing.##

The water gives you nothing back.# No resistance you can read, no direction,
nothing but its own black weight in every direction at once, and after five
or six strokes the pressure in your ears has gone from an ache to a hard,
insistent squeeze, which tells you exactly one thing, somewhat too late:
you have been swimming down.##

The last of your air leaves you in a rush you cannot stop, one fat mouthful
of it going somewhere you cannot see, and the cold closes over the panic
and puts it out like a candle.# You stop.# You have nothing left to spend,
and no way at all left to spend it.##

And your body, which has been trying to tell you something for rather longer
than you have been listening, is still trying.##

nodes.recap: find surface, then lose consciousness in water
nodes.text:
You stop fighting.# You go limp in the cold water
and let the darkness be still around you for one terrible second,
and then you feel it, the faint, slow pull of your body
toward one direction rather than another,
the physics of buoyancy asserting itself even here.##

You kick hard, toward where up should be.##

You break the surface with a gasp that tears at your throat, coughing water,
arms thrashing, and the rain hammers down
and the sea heaves around you in enormous dark swells,
and lightning flashes somewhere behind the clouds, illuminating for one white second
a field of wreckage, splintered wood, a torn sail panel, debris scattered
across the face of the water.##

You can see nothing.# You call out,
but the wind takes your voice and tears it to nothing.#
The cold is extraordinary, and your limbs are already growing heavy.##

Another wave, and you take a breath,
and then the sea takes you down again,
and the darkness comes back, and this time you do not fight it.##

You float.##

Down.##
